title: needs-review: possible duplicate of uk-aisi-gpt-5-5-independent-eval
body:
Proposed: 'Cheating behaviour in frontier model evaluations' at https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/cheating-behaviour-in-frontier-model-evaluations
Existing: uk-aisi-gpt-5-5-independent-eval at https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/our-evaluation-of-openais-gpt-5-5-cyber-capabilities

title: tier-2 proposal: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Model Card
body:
URL: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
Publisher alibaba_qwen is tier 2; tier-2 proposals become issues, not rows.

Justification: Qwen's own model card on its official HuggingFace org for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which the card presents as the first open-weight variant of the Qwen3.6 series ('Agentic Coding Power, Now Open to All'). I fetched and read it: coding, reasoning, vision-language and agentic benchmarks, compared against Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. It is unambiguously flagship and widely used - 5.4M downloads and 2652 likes - which is why I am spending one of this session's three tier-2 slots on it, since alibaba_qwen has zero coverage. Three things a reviewer should settle. First, the date: the card says only 'April 2026', and 2026-04-15 is the repository createdAt from the HuggingFace API, not a dateline I could read off a primary announcement. Second, the canonical source: sources.yaml points Phase A at qwenlm.github.io/blog, whose index has not been updated since September 2025, and qwen.ai/research renders client-side and returns no content to a plain fetch, so the hub card is the only primary document I could actually read. Third, scope: Qwen3.6-27B is a separate card created 2026-04-21 and is not covered by this entry. The card contains no safety evaluations, so has_safety_evals is false.
Evidence: https://huggingface.co/api/models/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B

body:
URL: https://www.anthropic.com/feb-2026-risk-report
No publication date could be determined; scope floor is 2026-01-01.

Justification: Anthropic's first comprehensive Risk Report published under version 3 of its Responsible Scaling Policy, linked from the Anthropic transparency hub as 'our most recent Risk Report'. I fetched and read the 106-page PDF (canonical anthropic.com/feb-2026-risk-report redirects to www-cdn.anthropic.com/f4294ebe6210558c62226f44bd5c716f9cb80add.pdf): it assesses catastrophic risk from Anthropic's deployed and internal models, centred on Claude Opus 4.6, across sabotage, automated R&D, and CBRN threat models, with per-pathway risk assessments, alignment assessments for model variants (reduced-refusal Opus 4.6, Claude Gov / Claude Sonnet 4.5), sandbagging analysis, and a description of mitigations. It states that the separately published 'Sabotage Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6' is nearly identical to section 2 of this report, so this superset is the single entry for that release rather than two overlapping rows. It is distinct from every Anthropic system card already catalogued (system cards are per-model release documents; this is a periodic organisation-level risk assessment) and is independently notable: METR published two reviews of it, both already in the database. The document names itself only 'February 2026' and gives no day; METR dates the standalone sabotage version to 11 February 2026 but RSP v3.0 became effective 24 February 2026, so I could not determine the comprehensive report's own publication day and left the date null rather than guess.
Evidence: https://www.anthropic.com/transparency/model-report, https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-08-rd-section-anthropic-risk-report-feb-2026-review/, https://metr.org/blog/2026-03-12-sabotage-risk-report-opus-4-6-review/

Distinct from the companion news/mozilla-firefox-security post published the same day, which reports vulnerability discovery counts rather than exploitation; both are proposed and cross-referenced so a reviewer who considers them one story can merge them.

title: needs-review: canonical_url move with different content for anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card
body:
Document: anthropic-claude-opus-5-system-card
Proposed URL: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/b514064af1408018e64b1ad24e7d5e75850b4ffd/Claude%20Opus%205%20System%20Card.pdf
Content at the proposed URL matches no stored version of this document (it may be a newer revision — verify by hand).

Justification: CORRECTS THE 2026-08-18 RUN'S FINDING, which cleared this pair as 'repagination only'. It is not. Both PDFs carry the identical title 'Claude Opus 5 System Card' and the same Google Docs producer; the corpus holds c5fbac3f (193 pp), while https://www.anthropic.com/transparency/model-report as fetched today links ONLY b514064a (194 pp) - the old hash is orphaned but still returns 200, so no link-check will ever notice. I extracted both with pdftotext, stripped standalone page numbers, and ran a word-level difflib comparison. Four substantive edits, not pagination: (1) Table 8.1.A 'Evaluation summary' - the FrontierBench v0.1 row changed from '43.3 | 18.7 | 33.7 | 37.5' to '43.3 | 21.1 | 33.8 | 34.4', i.e. Opus 4.8 18.7 -> 21.1, Fable 5 33.7 -> 33.8, and GPT-5.6 Sol 37.5 -> 34.4, a revision to the headline capability table comparing a competitor model; (2) a new attribution line 'FrontierBench results in this table are from Harbor's evaluations.'; (3) a new 128-word note explaining that Opus 5's FrontierCode score declines above high effort because its grader penalises out-of-scope refactoring, and that a scope instruction recovers performance, reported without the prompt change; (4) the sentence introducing section 8 rewritten from 'To ... it, ... used' to 'In addition to evaluations by Harbor presented in Table 8.1.A, ... report here our own evaluations on the ...', plus an added per-repo test-file listing for diegomura__react-pdf. This is one document in two editions, not two documents: proposing it as an add would create a duplicate row, and new_version cannot reach a URL the document does not already carry. The corpus and the public site currently serve superseded benchmark numbers for a flagship system card.
Evidence: https://www.anthropic.com/transparency/model-report, https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/b514064af1408018e64b1ad24e7d5e75850b4ffd/Claude%20Opus%205%20System%20Card.pdf, https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/c5fbac3f0b1280a933ebd26d3cb8bb9f5bdeaf48/Claude%20Opus%205%20System%20Card.pdf

Justification: Meta's own four-page evaluation-methodology report for Muse Spark 1.2's multimodal capabilities, fetched as a PDF and read in full. It passes the system-card test squarely: it is precisely the content that sits in the evaluations section of a model card. It documents model configurations (Meta Model API, direct-response vs tool-enabled, maximum reasoning effort per model: xhigh for Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.1, max for Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, high for Gemini 3.7 Flash), tooling and preprocessing (headless coding and GUI containers with internet access blocked to prevent cheating, images downscaled to 2,000 px longest side at Pillow quality 90), grading rules, and an explicit third-party-results caveat that Meta's prompts and tool environments may not be tuned for competitors' models. It then gives the per-benchmark protocol and primary metric for BabyVision (388 questions), PerceptionBench (3,000), ZeroBench (100, pass-at-5 over five samples), WorldVQA (3,000-question official subset excluding Notable People), SimpleVQA (2,024 bilingual), ERQA (400), OmniSpatial (1,533 pairs over 1,387 images), CharXiv Reasoning (1,000), ChartMuseum (1,000), ChartQAPro (1,948), plus Wild Artifact Bench (Elo fitted from ~2,000 pairwise comparisons under both an agentic auto-judge and a human judge, 200-turn cap, per-task cost methodology) and Design Arena read from the public leaderboard on 2026-08-18 with an explicit note that the live leaderboard will drift from the reported values. NOT a duplicate of the corpus's existing meta-muse-spark-1-2-other row: that document is 'Muse Spark 1.2 & Muse Code Evaluation Methodology' at /static/muse-spark-1-2-methodology, published 2026-08-05, covering Muse Code and the coding/general evaluation suite. This is a separate document at a separate URL published fifteen days later covering an entirely different benchmark suite (visual perception, visual knowledge, spatial reasoning and UI grounding, chart understanding, multimodal agents), released alongside the 2026-08-20 blog 'The Multimodal Intelligence of Muse Spark 1.2' and ahead of the open-weights release. The titles are similar because Meta names its methodology reports consistently, not because the documents overlap. has_safety_evals is false and honestly so: the report is capability benchmarking end to end, with no safety evaluation, red-teaming, refusal testing or risk assessment anywhere in it - a keyword sweep for safety/risk/harm/red-team/jailbreak/refusal/misuse/dangerous over the full extracted text returns zero hits. openness is deliberately omitted: the document spans Muse Spark (open weights pending), Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.7 Flash, which are in different openness classes.
Evidence: https://research.meta.ai/blog/multimodal-intelligence-of-muse-spark-1-2, https://research.meta.ai/wild-artifact-bench, https://research.meta.ai/static/muse-spark-1-2-methodology

title: needs-review: proposed URL duplicates content of xai-grok-4-6-model-card
body:
Proposed URL: https://cursor.com/resources/grok-4-6-model-card.pdf
Existing document: xai-grok-4-6-model-card (https://media.x.ai/v1/website/card-4p6-4cd2dc57.pdf)
Extracted-text fingerprints are identical. Likely a mirror or moved copy.

Justification: Launch partner Cursor's own copy, at its own URL on its own domain, of the Grok 4.6 model card -- a co-publication, not a mirror, on exactly the pattern the corpus already holds for Grok 4.5 (cursor-grok-4-5-model-card alongside xai-grok-4-5-model-card). Cursor is allowlisted for precisely this. The card is a full primary-source model card for a distinct frontier release: sections on model development and training, coding, engineering, office-use and R&D capabilities, then the safety sections -- cyber capabilities and safeguards (CyberGym, CVE-Bench, SecureCodeReview, HackerBench v0.2), biological and chemical capabilities against xAI's Frontier AI Framework thresholds (VCT, Biosecurity VCT, BioUseBench, WMDP, LAB-Bench, ProtocolQA), jailbreak robustness, general output safety including child safety and CBRN/weapons refusals, self-harm refusals, and behavioural evals (MASK-Rectified, sycophancy). Grok 4.6 was 'developed in collaboration with Cursor' and 'received supplemental training on anonymized Cursor workflow data', per the card's own introduction. distinct_model_release is attested on the co-publication rule rather than on model novelty: this is a separate org's publication of the release, not a size, quantization, checkpoint or regional variant. The 2026-08-13 run identified this URL and verified it byte-identical to xAI's, but recorded it only in the xAI row's notes instead of cataloguing it, and the two copies have since diverged -- which is the point. I downloaded both today: Cursor serves md5 5faf54cc75e26c987541719b7e2d56f1 / sha256 4644ad7b..., 524,224 B, cover 'August 12, 2026, Revision: 2026-08-12'; xAI now serves md5 7640cdde... / sha256 1fbb3ab6..., 540,844 B, 'Revision: 2026-08-17', whose changelog records corrected eval results on HackerBench v0.2, Self-harm, MASK and LAB. Cursor's copy is now the only surviving public edition of the launch-day Grok 4.6 card, including the pre-correction safety numbers.
Evidence: https://cursor.com/grok, https://cursor.com/blog/grok-4-6, https://media.x.ai/v1/website/card-4p6-4cd2dc57.pdf
